 By Natalie Dreier, Cox Media Group National Content Desk November 03, 2026 at 10:43 am EST Enter Fullscreen Expand Recall alert FILE PHOTO: Olmesartan Medoxomil, Amlodipine, and Hydrochlorothiazide tablets have been recalled. (CH. HORZ/Christian Horz - stock.adobe.com) By Natalie Dreier, Cox Media Group National Content Desk November 03, 2026 at 10:43 am EST If you take blood pressure medication, you will need to check your prescriptions. The Food and Drug Administration announced the recall of a popular treatment. 
 Read more trending news The agency said Olmesartan Medoxomil, Amlodipine, and Hydrochlorothiazide tablets have been recalled. 
 The Mayo Clinic said the pill is a combination of medications that can be used alone or in combination with others for high blood pressure. 
 Olmesartan is an angiotensin II receptor blocker, while Amlodipine is a calcium channel blocker, and Hydrochlorothiazide is a diuretic, the Mayo Clinic said.
 They failed to meet dissolution specifications. 
 The recall affects two lots: 2251163A, expiration date 05-31-2027 and 12251163B, expiration date 05-31-2027. They were dispensed nationwide.
 The FDA said the recall affects 3,528 30-count bottles and 216 90-count bottles. 
 The medications were initially recalled on Oct. 7, but the FDA classified it as a Class II recall on Oct. 26. 
 A Class II recall is “a situation in which use of or exposure to a violative product may cause temporary or medically reversible adverse health consequences or where the probability of serious adverse health consequences is remote.”
